sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《构筑新视角》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及围绕其展开的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚都会带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，摆满了美丽的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在可以在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《构筑新视角》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》播客，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Thousands of Haitians seeking refuge in the United States are being turned away at the border and deported without being given a chance to apply for asylum
sentences.zh: 数千名在美利坚合众国寻求庇护的海地人在边境被拒之门外，并在没有机会申请庇护的情况下被驱逐出境

sentences.en: at a moment when their country is less stable and less safe than ever.
sentences.zh: 而此时他们的国家比以往任何时候都更加不稳定、更加不安全。

sentences.en: Asted Herndon spoke to our colleague, Mike Scheer, about why that's happening.
sentences.zh: 阿斯特德·赫恩登就此事为什么会发生采访了我们的同事迈克·希尔。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月27日，星期一。

sentences.en: So tell me what's been going on at the border along Del Rio and Texas.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我德尔里奥和得克萨斯州边界究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: The crisis on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: southern border deepens tonight.
sentences.zh: 南部边境的危机今晚进一步加深。

sentences.en: So about 10 days ago or so, the border in Del Rio, which is in Texas, suddenly found itself kind of overwhelmed by a group of Haitians.
sentences.zh: 大约10天前，位于得克萨斯州的德尔里奥边境突然发现自己被一群海地人挤得水泄不通。

sentences.en: There are those thousands of migrants who have set up this makeshift camp.
sentences.zh: 有成千上万的难民搭建了这个临时营地。

sentences.en: Most of whom had traveled from, some from Haiti itself, but many from different parts of South America where they had been living, with the hope of getting into the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分人是从海地本土出发的，但也有许多人来自南美洲的不同地区，他们此前一直在那里生活，怀揣着进入美国的希望。

sentences.en: And within a matter of days...
sentences.zh: 短短几天之内……

sentences.en: There are still more than 10,000 migrants.
sentences.zh: 这里依然有超过1万名难民。

sentences.en: 12,000 migrants.
sentences.zh: 1万2千名难民。
1万3千名。

sentences.en: We're talking about nearly 15,000 migrants here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里讨论的是将近15,000名难民。

sentences.en: You know, what started out as a few hundred migrants had swelled to thousands.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一开始只是几百名难民，后来激增到了数千人。

sentences.en: This is what the U.S.'s immigration waiting room looks like in Del Rio, Texas.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国在得克萨斯州德尔里奥的移民候车室的现状。

sentences.en: We're told that they've been sleeping on the dirt, surrounded by trash, out here in this hot Texas sun.
sentences.zh: 我们得知他们一直睡在泥土地上，四周环绕着垃圾，顶着得克萨斯州炙热的太阳。

sentences.en: Kind of hemmed in in this squalid, makeshift camp.
sentences.zh: 被困在这个肮脏简陋的临时营地里。

sentences.en: And with food and supplies constantly running short.
sentences.zh: 而且食物和物资经常短缺。

sentences.en: Which then, of course, drew the notice of, you know, the administration, the border patrol, the people who have to figure out what to do about this.
sentences.zh: 这自然引起了政府、边境巡逻队以及那些必须想办法解决这一问题的人们的注意。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: Thousands of Haitian migrants are now being deported.
sentences.zh: 数千名海地难民现在正被驱逐出境。

sentences.en: What they decided to do was to, in some cases, ship people back, put them on planes and fly them to Haiti.
sentences.zh: 他们决定的做法在某些情况下是将人们送回，让他们登上飞机飞往海地。

sentences.en: In other cases, you know, put them on buses.
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，你知道的，把他们送上大巴。

sentences.en: Some were taken into custody.
sentences.zh: 有些人被拘留了。

sentences.en: Some were released to come back for court cases later.
sentences.zh: 有些人被释放，以便日后出庭应诉。

sentences.en: And, of course, the thing that really caught the attention of everybody was...
sentences.zh: 当然，真正引起所有人注意的是……

sentences.en: Okay, I want to show you some unbelievable images shot near Del Rio, Texas.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想向你们展示一些在得克萨斯州德尔里奥附近拍摄的难以置信的画面。

sentences.en: In the middle of all of this, where border patrol agents, some of them were on horseback,
sentences.zh: 在这一切的中心，边境巡逻特工骑着马，

sentences.en: chasing after Haitian migrants,
sentences.zh: 追赶海地难民，

sentences.en: grabbing them by the cuff of the neck, and, in some cases, using the reins from the horses to sort of catch them.
sentences.zh: 抓住他们的衣领，有时甚至用马缰绳来试图抓住他们。

sentences.en: Why are you whipping them?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么要鞭打他们？

sentences.en: Why are you not offering care?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么不提供救助？

sentences.en: You know, these images, they're so horrific.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些画面太可怕了。

sentences.en: All of which generated a lot of attention and controversy on the way the administration responded to the situation.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切在政府对局势的反应方式上引发了极大的关注和争议。

sentences.en: These horrifying images seem far more reminiscent of the Fugitive Slave Acts of the 1790s and 1850, and not 2021.
sentences.zh: 这些可怕的画面让人极其强烈地想起1790年代和1850年的《逃亡奴隶法》，而不是2021年。

sentences.en: I am ashamed that this is how Americans are treating other immigrants.
sentences.zh: 我为美国人这样对待其他移民感到羞耻。

sentences.en: The world is watching.
sentences.zh: 全世界都在看着。

sentences.en: Right, it feels like kind of the image of the last week.
sentences.zh: 没错，这感觉就像是过去这一周的标志性画面。

sentences.en: We saw that border patrol on the horseback, using those reins in this kind of, like, whip-like fashion, and rounding these folks up, and that was shared far and wide.
sentences.zh: 我们看到骑马的边境巡逻人员用那种鞭子一样的缰绳把这些人赶在一起，这在各处广为流传。

sentences.en: But why did so many thousands of Haitian migrants come to the border all at once in the first place?
sentences.zh: 但为什么会有成千上万的海地难民突然一起涌向边境呢？

sentences.en: How did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: You know, it's always a challenge to sort of point to one reason.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要想指出某一个原因总是很难。

sentences.en: President Biden had recently extended a sort of designation for Haitians who are already living in the United States that allows them to live and work here legally
sentences.zh: 拜登总统最近延长了对已经在美国生活的海地人的一种身份认定，允许他们在美合法居住和工作

sentences.en: for another period of time.
sentences.zh: 一段时间。

sentences.en: These are largely Haitians that had fled the devastating earthquake in 2010 and other political and sort of natural disasters in that country, and had been living here
sentences.zh: 这些人主要是为逃离2010年毁灭性地震以及该国其他政治和自然灾害而来到这里的海地人，他们一直生活在

sentences.en: under the protection of a law that is known as temporary protected status.
sentences.zh: 被称为“临时保护身份”的法律保护之下。

sentences.en: And Donald Trump, during the last four years, had tried to sort of turn off that protection and send a lot of Haitians home.
sentences.zh: 在过去四年里，唐纳德·特朗普曾试图取消这种保护，并将许多海地人遣送回国。

sentences.en: President Biden, when he came in, said, no, no, no, that's not, we're not doing that.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统上台后表示，不，不，不，这不是我们要做的。

sentences.en: We're going to extend the protections for these people.
sentences.zh: 我们要为这些人延长保护期。

sentences.en: So one theory, I think, among administration officials and others who watch this is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为政府官员和密切关注此事的人士当中的一种看法是，

sentences.en: Haitians who might have been living in South America, had fled maybe the country in the past, sort of heard about that decision by President Biden and thought,
sentences.zh: 可能曾住在南美洲、过去曾逃离祖国的海地人听说了拜登总统的这一决定，便认为，

sentences.en: oh, well, if it's more lenient now, maybe I can come and I can stay in the United States too.
sentences.zh: 哦，既然现在更宽松了，也许我也能来美国待着。

sentences.en: Now, the truth is, the change that President Biden made would not have affected those people because it only applies to people who had already been living in the United States.
sentences.zh: 然而事实是，拜登总统做出的改变并不会影响那些人，因为它只适用于已经在美国生活的人。

sentences.en: But it's certainly possible that they misunderstood the implications of his decision and that that convinced folks to come.
sentences.zh: 但他们肯定有可能误解了他这一决定的含义，从而说服了人们前来。

sentences.en: So that's the theory number one, the kind of cause and effect that the Biden administration's change in the policy, specifically around folks who are already here,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是第一种理论，即因果关系，认为拜登政府政策的改变，特别是针对那些已经在这里的人，

sentences.en: that temporary protective status, that the word might have gotten out and encouraged people who were not in the United States to come here,
sentences.zh: 即那个临时保护身份，这个消息可能已经传开，并鼓励了不在美国本土的人来到这里，

sentences.en: even though it technically didn't apply to them.
sentences.zh: 尽管从技术上讲这并不适用他们。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And there is, I mean, the other thing to point to, I suppose, is that there obviously has been terrible times in Haiti recently.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，另一件可以指出的事情是，海地最近显然经历了一段糟糕的时期。

sentences.en: You've had another earthquake, you had political instability with the assassination of the country's president.
sentences.zh: 你们经历了一场又一场地震，随着该国总统遇刺，你们还遭遇了政治动荡。

sentences.en: So if there were Haitians who were living either in the country at the time or already in South America, but contemplating, gee, am I ever going to be able to go back to my home
sentences.zh: 因此，如果有些海地人当时要么住在国内，要么已经身在南美，但却在琢磨，天哪，我还能不能回到我的家乡

sentences.en: and, you know, kind of start over?
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，重新开始？

sentences.en: If the recent strife in that country convinced them that they weren't going to be able to go home anytime soon, maybe some of them saw the United States as a second option.
sentences.zh: 如果该国最近的冲突让他们确信自己短期内无法回国，也许他们中的一些人将美国视为第二个选择。

sentences.en: And so some of them, the intent is to apply, for example, for asylum, saying that they, you know, deserve to be, have refuge here in the United States
sentences.zh: 因此，他们中的一些人，其意图是申请庇护，例如声称他们，你知道，应当获得在美国的庇护

sentences.en: from the country that they left.
sentences.zh: 来逃离他们离开的国家。

sentences.en: Others, I think, are just hoping that they will be allowed to stay.
sentences.zh: 我想，另一些人只是希望他们能被允许留下来。

sentences.en: The problem is that that runs headfirst into the interests of the Biden administration and the government, which, you know, has as its sort of basic tenet that, you know,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这与拜登政府和政府的利益直接相撞，后者，你知道的，其基本原则之一就是，

sentences.en: you don't come into the United States illegally.
sentences.zh: 你不能非法进入美国。

sentences.en: That's not the proper way.
sentences.zh: 这不是正确的方式。

sentences.en: And so the United States has, even under the Biden administration, has a series of rules that allows them to determine what to do with people who just simply cross the Rio Grande
sentences.zh: 因此，即使在拜登政府领导下，美国仍有一系列规则，允许他们决定如何处理那些直接穿过格兰德河

sentences.en: and come into the United States.
sentences.zh: 并进入美国的人。

sentences.en: And many of those rules allow the United States at this point to just turn these people back, send them home.
sentences.zh: 其中许多规则允许美国在现阶段直接将这些人驱逐回去，送他们回国。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But we also know that there are legal ways of entering the country, like applying for asylum.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，有合法的入境途径，比如申请庇护。

sentences.en: So why are these people getting turned away?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这些人会被拒之门外呢？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's complicated, but the Biden administration has kept in place a rule that former President Trump invoked at the beginning of the pandemic
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，情况很复杂，但拜登政府保留了一条前总统特朗普在疫情初期实施的规则，

sentences.en: in the early days of 2020, a rule intended to be a public health rule that basically said, we have the authority to keep anybody out of our country if we think
sentences.zh: 即2020年初的早期，这条本意为公共卫生规则的条款基本上规定，如果我们认为任何人

sentences.en: they're a potential threat to the public health of the United States.
sentences.zh: 对美国的公共卫生构成潜在威胁，我们就有权将其拒之国门之外。

sentences.en: That essentially
sentences.zh: 这本质上

sentences.en: overwrites the asylum rules that are normally in place.
sentences.zh: 凌驾于通常生效的庇护规则之上。

sentences.en: So when the Biden administration came in, one of the big questions was, would the Biden administration stop using that particular public health rule in order to keep the border
sentences.zh: 因此，当拜登政府上台时，最大的问题之一是：拜登政府会停止使用那项特定的公共卫生规则，以便使边境

sentences.en: more welcoming back to the way it had been prior to that, which allowed people to claim asylum?
sentences.zh: 恢复到以前那种允许人们申请庇护的更受欢迎的状态吗？

sentences.en: The surprising thing to many is that the Biden administration did not choose to stop using that public health rule.
sentences.zh: 令许多人感到惊讶的是，拜登政府并没有选择停止使用该公共卫生规则。

sentences.en: In fact, they kept it in place.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们将其保留了下来。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, the truth is that the administration understood that if they dropped that rule, they were going to be facing more surges like this across the border of people trying
sentences.zh: 好吧，事实是，政府明白，如果他们放弃这项规则，他们将面临更多企图跨越边境进入美国的人潮，

sentences.en: to get into the United States.
sentences.zh: 就像这样一波又一波的冲击。

sentences.en: And until they were ready to deal with that, until they'd managed to rebuild the immigration system so that it could handle those increased numbers of people, they wanted to keep
sentences.zh: 在他们准备好应对之前，在他们设法重建移民系统以使其能够应付不断增加的人数之前，他们希望将其

sentences.en: it in place.
sentences.zh: 保持在原位。

sentences.en: And that's sort of the reason.
sentences.zh: 这就是原因所在。

sentences.en: In other words, they're also worried about encouraging waves of migrants, just like President Trump was.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们也和特朗普总统一样，担心助长难民潮。

sentences.en: So under Biden, this public health rule is still functioning as a policy of deterrence.
sentences.zh: 所以在拜登领导下，这项公共卫生规则依然作为一种威慑政策在起作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So at the end of all this, you have these, frankly, awful images of white men on horseback rounding up
sentences.zh: 所以在这一切的最后，你看到了这些坦率说来极其糟糕的画面：白人骑警在四处围捕

sentences.en: Black migrants in an effort to forcibly remove them from the country.
sentences.zh: 黑人难民，企图将他们强行驱逐出境。

sentences.en: and people and Democrats are left wondering why are we seeing images in the
sentences.zh: 而民众和民主党人不禁在想，为什么我们在

sentences.en: Biden administration that so many
sentences.zh: 拜登政府治下看到的画面

sentences.en: Democrats rejected under the Trump administration?
sentences.zh: 竟然和民主党人在特朗普政府治下强烈反对的如出一辙？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，你说的完全对。

sentences.en: Look, this is a president, a presidential candidate who called the former president's immigration approach inhuman.
sentences.zh: 听着，这是一位曾经称前总统的移民政策为不人道的总统、曾经的总统候选人。

sentences.en: And when you look at the scenes that we saw over the last two weeks or so, it really does leave you with the same question.
sentences.zh: 当你回顾过去两周左右我们看到的那些场景时，它确实会让你产生同样的疑问。

sentences.en: You know, how could you see the same kinds of brutal images, the same kinds of aggressive tactics being used against immigrants, against migrants by this president?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这位总统怎么能允许对移民、对难民使用同样残暴的画面、同样具有攻击性的战术呢？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚都会带着

sentences.zh: 300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，摆满了美丽的

sentences.en: 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 50年历史的艺术品。
